measure_ballots: Total ballots counted, the same column for 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022.
ballots_source: Michael McDonald, UF Election Lab, Turnout 1980–2022 v1.2, field TOTAL_BALLOTS_COUNTED. United States row is not used; the page sums the 50 states and D.C.
house_source: FEC Federal Elections reports, general-election votes for U.S. House candidates by party. A blank party cell is stored as 0 (no votes reported for that party). Territories are not in this table. The national FEC total, which includes D.C. and territories, stays in the national section.
house_2026_gap: 2026 House votes are the latest AP counts on the NBC News House results page, summed by party across every district, pulled 8:58 AM PT Nov. 7, 2026 (11:58 AM ET). Percent in is the vote-weighted share of expected vote; the lowest district is also kept. They are not certified. A count that came in lower than the Nov. 6 file was not applied: Texas House other stayed 43,622 (NBC 43,583) and Vermont's House totals stayed at the Nov. 6 figures. Florida's 10th District is still 0 votes in the feed, so its weighted percent ignores that empty district and the minimum is 0. D.C. has no voting House seat; its count is the attorney general race. Indiana, Missouri, North Dakota and Washington have no 2026 governor or Senate race, so the top line is the highest statewide contest on the NBC state page. Utah's top line is the House sum. Oregon and West Virginia also have an official ballots-counted figure, which the table uses instead of the contest. The national total is the sum of the 50 states.
